name: WhiteDB
tagline: Shared-memory C database library storing typed N-tuples, readable by many processes at once; archived.
description: WhiteDB is a lightweight NoSQL database library in C that keeps all data in a shared memory segment, so several processes can read and write the same database directly without a server or sockets, and the data survives after they exit. Records are N-tuples of encoded fields (integers, strings, doubles, dates, or links to other records), with T-tree indexes, a query API, logging and disk dumps for durability, Python bindings and experimental Java bindings. It was developed by Tanel Tammet and Priit Järv with an eye to RDF and rule-engine workloads. The last stable release is 0.7.3 (2014); the maintainers stopped building releases and archived the repository in 2026.
statusNote: GitHub repo archived in 2026; maintainers no longer build releases (last stable 0.7.3, Nov 2014; 0.8.0alpha 2022).

scale.notes: Bounded by the size of one machine's shared memory segment.

strengths: Many processes share one in-memory database with no server or IPC overhead
Data persists in shared memory even when no process is attached
Very small footprint, portable C, Linux and Windows support
weaknesses: GPLv3 licence limits embedding in closed products
Limited to one machine's RAM; durability depends on dumps and logs
useCases: Fast shared state between local processes
Research on in-memory RDF and reasoning
